📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

Plenty of content has been migrating to streaming services for years now, but some of the most popular programming is still only available on traditional TV. From sports like NFL, college football, and NBA games to awards shows, some content is still most easily accessible via a traditional channel guide.

Luckily, if you don’t want a traditional cable or satellite package, there are now a handful of standout live TV streaming services that beat those dying cable boxes with better pricing, more streamlined packages, and viewing flexibility.

One of those standout live TV streaming services is Fubo. The popular service offers hundreds of channels in a selection of well-priced packages. If you’re looking to ditch cable — or find a way to access channels you lost by cutting the cord — it’s a great option.

Fubo offers more than 250 channels in its top-tier subscription. These channels include network stations ABC, CBS, and FOX, plus all of the most popular cable channels and regional sports networks (in certain packages). Cable channels include standouts like ESPN, FS1, Fox News, MSNBC, HGTV, CNN, Bravo, and Hallmark Channel. The only notable absence on Fubo is TNT. See Fubo’s full channel lineup here.

Fubo plans start at $64.99 a month, and the service’s most expensive package is $98.99 a month. Similar top-tier packages from other streamers can easily surpass $100 a month, making Fubo’s pricing very competitive.

Here’s a quick breakdown of Fubo’s (English-language) package offerings:.

Sports + News: Fubo’s Sports + News plan is a streamlined, affordable option that costs $64.99 a month. You get 30+ channels, including local stations (ABC, CBS, NBC, and FOX), Fox News, and sports channels like ESPN, FS1, and NFL Network.

Sources indicate that pro: Fubo’s Pro strategy costs $88.99 a month and offers a great balance of price and channel availability. It includes local channels, regional sports networks, cable sports channels, news stations, and a huge selection of entertainment channels.

In a recent development, elite: Fubo’s largest package is Elite, which offers over 250 channels and — unlike the options above — 4K UHD high-resolution streaming for certain content. It costs $98.99 a month.

Recent findings suggest that another important note: all Fubo packages offer unlimited DVR recording and streaming on up to 10 screens at a time. That’s a better deal than any other live TV streaming service, and frankly, it’s shocking that both perks are available in all packages.

Fubo is at the moment offering deals on all of its plans. Latest consumers can get a discount of up to $30 off their first month, depending on the initiative they select. You can get $25 off your first month with the Pro plan and $30 off your first month with the Elite plan.

When Apple unveiled its new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR last month, it highlighted several big updates coming to Apple Creator Studio’s app suite.

Updates for Pages, Keynote, and Numbers are rolling out too with an Intelligent Assistant feature, as well as smaller releases for Apple’s other pro utilities.

Latest Update: The Best Music Moments and Surprise Cameos From ‘GTA VI’

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here.
  • In a recent development, once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts.
  • Recent findings suggest that the game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here. Music, of course, is integral to all of it. There’s a soundtrack full of stars — the 34-track release, which is out today, features Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Arca, and more. In addition to that, there is a massive one-day festival inspired by the game, taking place in Miami on Nov. 21, with headliners Cardi B, Metro Boomin, and Justice, who also put together the game’s score.

In a recent development, once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts. Here are some of the best music moments and surprise cameos from the biggest video game of the year.

Recent findings suggest that the game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back. There’s Cocoteo FM hosted by Bad Bunny and RaiNao, Back Country Radio hosted by Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey, and Radio La Ola with Gloria and Emilio Estefan, plus tons more. But one that may surprise people is Stockyard FM, featuring two DJs named Victoria and Harrison — better known as PinkPantheress and the Dare. Victoria and Harrison are their real names, and their radio station is dedicated to experimental, left-of-center pop, electronica, and indie sleaze.

In a recent development, one of the GTA VI radio stations, Radio La Ola, plays homage to Latin classics from over the decades. But one hugely surprising one is “Sopa de Caracol,” a massive but somewhat forgotten hit from the Nineties by Honduran band Banda Blanca. The inclusion made headlines in Central America, with the lead singer Pilo Tejada saying he was honored to have his voice reach new parts of the world.

Psych-rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard is featured on the soundtrack: They’re one of several artists on the collaboration “Flower in a Hurricane,” which also earned them their first Billboard 100 entry. But that’s not the only place you can find them: Gizz fans noticed that throughout several parts of the game, you can hear snippets of what appear to be demos from the band, woven into the score. On Reddit, diehards have been pointing these out and playing guessing games as they wonder what projects these might be from.

We’ve known that the French electronic duo Justice composed the original score for the game, but the official album won’t be out until Dec. 11. We’re getting to hear some of what they came up with the release of the game but there’s still more to come, including an anticipated collaboration with the Weeknd. The duo have since noted this is the “first and last” video game they’ll ever score.

Sources indicate that the soundtrack, which dropped on Nov. 19, is packed, featuring 34 songs by some surprising artists and stars. There’s new music from Travis Scott, the Fuerza Regida track “Suzuki,” which is charting in 15 countries, and there are also songs from Keith Richards, Kali Uchis and Helado Negro, and more. A lot of the music was inspired directly by Miami, which you can hear in new tracks from artists like JT.

Artists are getting into the game, too. Tinashe delighted fans with a hilarious livestream playing for the first time. The stream captured her making an epic getaway by flying an airplane and hysterically crashing it into the ground, then running out of ammo in a shootout. “I have no bullets!” she screams. “Holy shit, I’m going to have to beat the fuck out of them myself.” After several days of sold-out shows in the U.K., Noah Kahan stayed up late and wreaked havoc in Vice City while his wife was asleep.

It has been revealed that the world lost D’Angelo back in 2025, but his legacy lives on in Vice City. GTA VI players discovered that an unreleased track called “Kamakazi,” as confirmed by D’Angelo collaborator DJ Dojah, is one of the songs you can hear on the radio station Worldwide FM. D’Angelo’s “Lady” also plays on the in-game Honey FM channel, which is hosted by Chilli and T-Boz of TLC.

While the creators of the game spent a ton of time adding interesting radio stations and track to the GTA VI universe, there is plenty of love for pop stars and major pop hits. Dua Lipa appears on the soundtrack, but the radio stations also feature plenty of pop girlies: There’s Chappell Roan’s “Hot To Go!,” Charli XCX’s “Good Ones,” and Addison Rae’s “Fame Is a Gun,” just to name a few, which players can blast while driving through Vice City.

Industry observers note that chatGPT dictation is getting a boost today. OpenAI has updated the speech-to-text feature with Live Dictation that improves both speed and reliability. The enhanced dictation upgrade also removes the 10-minute limit.

“Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable,” OpenAI declared on X.

“With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing,” the company continued.

Atty Eleti, who works on voice features at OpenAI, added that the 10-minute dictation limit has also been removed as part of the dictation streaming upgrade.

More details from today’s app revision release notes below:.

Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable.

According to recent reports, with Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. Tap or click on the waveform to show or hide text as you go. We’ve also removed the 10-minute recording limit.

Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web, and the desktop app.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rosalía gushed that it was an “honor” for Taylor Swift to hail her Grammy-nominated Lux as a “perfect album” and said that she considers the pop star a “master songwriter.”.

In a recent development, “To me, she’s a master, honestly,” Rosalía noted during a red carpet interview for the Los40 Music Awards in Barcelona on Friday. “I think she’s incredible.” The Spanish singer also revealed her favorite Swift track. “I prefer individual songs rather than albums,” she added. “There’s one I really love, “Wildest Dreams.” It’s one of the songs I’ve listened to the most in my entire life.”.

Swift had sung Rosalía’s praise earlier this month during a press conference for the nominations for the Golden Globes, which she is up for Best Original Song for the Toy Story 5 track, “I Knew It, I Knew You.”   Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis.

Industry observers note that “Two perfect albums that I love and that I kept coming back to are from Olivia Dean and Rosalía,” Swift shared about what will likely end up on her Spotify Wrapped this year. “For Rosalía, she has created an ambitious and expansive concept album that could’ve only come from her vital life experience. Those albums are marvelous because they’re human, they’re made for people and are about the human experience; that’s why humans connect with them.”.

The women’s camaraderie and mutual respect comes ahead of the 2027 Grammys where both are going up against each other in several categories, including Album of the Year for Rosalía’s classically experiment Lux and Swift’s glitzy The Life of a Showgirl, as well as Record of the Year for “Berghain” and “The Fate of Ophelia.”.

According to recent reports, sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon, and other retailers have been churning out early Black Friday deals since last week, so if you haven't been paying attention, you've already missed out on some good deals. But all hope is not lost: Costco recently started its own early sale, so you're still in time to find something you want at a low price. Below, I've rounded up my favorite tech deals from their sale—but keep in mind you'll need a membership to take advantage of these deals.

Industry observers note that A powerful monitor with high-end specs can make gaming more immersive and greatly reduce input lag, which is helpful for any serious gamer looking for an edge over their opponents. The Samsung Odyssey G9 is a 49-inch gaming monitor with some impressive specs, including a 240Hz refresh rate and a 1 ms response time. It's available for $699.99 (originally $899.99), $200 off and the lowest price it has reached this year.

If you're looking for a more premium (and far more massive) gaming monitor, the 57-inch Samsung Odyssey Neo G9, one of the best ultra-wide gaming monitors on the market, is at the moment on sale for $1,449.99 ($2,499.99 at launch). This monitor came out in 2023, earning an "excellent" review from PCMag for its impressive 7,680 x 2,160 4K resolution, its great color range and accuracy, a 240Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and its overall design. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful graphics card. But if you have the right setup, this thing really delivers.

It has been revealed that the 15.3-inch Lenovo Legion is a powerful gaming laptop with premium specs, and with the current $600 discount, it's down to $1999.99 (originally $2,599.99). It has a powerful AMD Ryzen AI 9 processor, 32 GB of RAM, a GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, and 1TB of SSD. PCMag gave the more affordable 5i version an excellent review for its price and performance, so if you have the cash for it, this one is even better.

A soundbar is a great way to improve a home entertainment system without spending too much money. This 5.1 TCL Q6CH setup is right now $199.99 (originally $299.99), including a soundbar and subwoofer. This soundbar came out in 2024 and supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X for that 3D sound, as well as AI Sonic, a tool that tunes your sound settings based on the setup of your room.

Sources indicate that the latest AirPods Pro are a major step up from their previous generation. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds deliver a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation: They're $179 at Costco (originally $249) in an early Black Friday deal.

Sources indicate that the 15-inch MacBook Air is down to $1,249 (originally $1,499), the lowest price since Apple hiked prices this past summer. The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a newly introduced machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Air, the M5 base model has double the storage, and the powerful M5 chip makes the performance even smoother, according to Mashable's review. The aluminum design is as good as you'd expect from Apple's most popular portable laptop, and it includes a Liquid Retina display, Touch ID, a 12MP Center Stage Camera, and the Magic Keyboard.

Industry observers note that the 15.6-inch Acer Aspire Go is a great value at its current $499.99 price (originally $699.99). The display is a touchscreen; it sports an AMD Ryzen 5 processor and it has 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. These aren't specs you normally find at this price, making it a great laptop for anyone looking to stretch their money as far as possible while getting a workhorse of a laptop.

It has been revealed that I'm a fan of TCL TVs, and right now own the "non-pro" version of this TV. The 65-inch QM6K Pro is $599.99 (originally $999.99) and has the same internal hardware and Mini-LED panel as the regular QM6K, but it adds a CrystGlow anti-reflective coating that makes it more viewable in well-lit rooms and helps maintain a high picture contrast. 3-legged Persian leopard's 150-mile journey highlights Caucasus border hazards

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mongabay

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that an endangered Persian leopard that researchers have named Aren recently completed a 240-kilometer (150-mile) journey through the snow-bound Caucasus Mountains that straddle Russia, Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan.
  • In a recent development, persian leopards (Panthera pardus tulliana) are endangered, with fewer than 1,044 individuals remaining worldwide, according to the IUCN, the global wildlife conservation authority.
  • Sources indicate that long’s reporting for Mongabay highlighted Aren’s trek, which was first identified by camera traps in Armenia’s Arpa Protected Area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that an endangered Persian leopard that researchers have named Aren recently completed a 240-kilometer (150-mile) journey through the snow-bound Caucasus Mountains that straddle Russia, Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan. Aren not just navigated a landscape that still contains decades-old minefields from prior conflicts, but he did so on just three legs. His journey highlights the severe hazards that border minefields and fencing pose to wildlife, Mongabay contributor Kayleigh Long told host Mike DiGirolamo on a recent episode of the Mongabay newscast.

In a recent development, persian leopards (Panthera pardus tulliana) are endangered, with fewer than 1,044 individuals remaining worldwide, according to the IUCN, the global wildlife conservation authority. In the past two decades, scientists have documented just three leopard sightings in Georgia and 10 in Armenia.

Sources indicate that long’s reporting for Mongabay highlighted Aren’s trek, which was first identified by camera traps in Armenia’s Arpa Protected Area. He started off as a healthy four-legged male, but when rangers spotted him months later, the lower part of his left foreleg was missing — an injury Arpa rangers say may have been inflicted by an antipersonnel mine along the border of Nakhchivan, an Azerbaijani exclave.

Such injuries are common in the region. According to WWF Armenia, three of the 10 leopards recorded in Armenia since 2002 have lost a limb. Soviet-era electric signal fences known as Sistema, along with modern border barriers, further obstruct movement across Iran, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia.

Industry observers note that “Leopards do not recognize political boundaries,” Hana Raza, founder of the nonprofit Leopards Beyond Borders, told Long. “Their survival depends on connected habitats and the ability to move safely across landscapes.”.

Raza added that mined areas make conservation harder by hindering monitoring and directly harming wildlife.

However, Aren, lacking one limb, adapted his hunting technique by lurking in cave mouths to ambush prey like bezoar goats (Capra aegagrus aegagrus). Arpa head ranger Samvel Karapetyan described Aren to Long as thriving and “fat.” He eventually traveled northward through Armenia and crossed into Georgia’s Algeti National Park, where a deer-monitoring camera recorded his presence in September 2025.

Long said conservation groups monitoring these elusive cats face severe resource constraints. Georgian NGO NACRES (Centre for Biodiversity Conservation & Research) operates on a skeleton crew led by zoologist Bejan Lortkipanidze amid global funding shortages.

Still, the persistence of massive cats like Aren offers a vital reason for optimism, Long added.

“When you look at things like borders, they can reflect the very worst of our instincts,” she stated. “Or if people are able to cooperate and recognize that we are a part of nature … we all have to get along with nature and with each other. In times like this, I sort of think hope is a moral imperative.”.

Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.
  • In a recent development, jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.
  • “Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” stated Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.

In a recent development, jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Federal prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of intentionally starting the original blaze, known as the Lachman fire. While the initial fire was quickly suppressed, unbeknownst to firefighters and other authorities at the time, embers of it continued to burn underground. On Jan. 7, heavy winds reignited the fire, causing it to surface and spread. The ensuing Palisades fire was one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people and decimating 23,448 acres of land and nearly 7,000 structures across the Pacific Palisades region.

“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” stated Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”.

According to recent reports, “Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”.

After a federal jury in June deadlocked in favor of acquittal in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June, federal prosecutors narrowed their case to charge him with the two arson-related felonies rather than the three charges in the mistrial.

It has been revealed that steve Haney, the man’s lawyer for both trials, told the Los Angeles Times that they planned to appeal Friday’s verdict. “We are disappointed in the verdict, but respect the jury process,” Haney told the publication. “After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration.” Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The prosecution argued that Rinderknecht, who was working on Fresh Year’s Eve as an Uber driver on Dec. 31, 2024, was angry and frustrated because he was unable to find companionship on New Year’s. According to an affidavit from an investigator for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, two of his passengers described him as “agitated and angry” that night. He allegedly drove to a Pacific Palisades trailhead, where he repeatedly listened to and watched a music video for the rap song, “Un Zder, Un Thé,” about despair, and tried calling an old friend, but was unable to connect with them.Prosecutors said that Rinderknecht started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, and that around 12:12 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman fire had begun. They said that Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of range. By the time he finally connected with the police, the fire had already been reported by others in the neighborhood.

During his call with police, per the affidavit, Rinderknecht also allegedly typed a question into ChatGPT: “Are you at fault if a fire is lift [sic] because of your cigarette?” ChatGPT allegedly responded “Yes.”.

#51256. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer indicates it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big challenges.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer indicates it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big challenges.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he indicates he has identified the next big shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Ng’s current efforts are focused on his manufacturer Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he notes can yield “small data” solutions to big issues in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

In a recent development, the great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

In a recent development, andrew Ng: This is a big question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

It has been revealed that ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a latest paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

It has been revealed that ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of consumers, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing manufacturer with millions of people.

According to recent reports, ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from massive data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

Sources indicate that I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and mentioned, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing new here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

Sources indicate that ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and remarked, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

In a recent development, the data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one tech giant or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that demonstrated up.

Sources indicate that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from significant data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

When you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand fresh model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Industry observers note that ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having noted that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For big data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

Recent findings suggest that for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very rapidly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

Could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Sources indicate that ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Newly introduced tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an vital piece of the puzzle.

It has been revealed that one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

Ng: In AI, data cleaning is important, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention promptly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

Industry observers note that for example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

Ng: I think synthetic data is an important tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

Recent findings suggest that “In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion owners. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

It has been revealed that synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

Sources indicate that to make these concerns more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a manufacturer approaches Landing AI and claims it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

Ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Sources indicate that ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and update the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion owners. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Recent findings suggest that ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent fresh neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s vital for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

It has been revealed that ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print matter as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, E.J. Carroll, a veteran character actor whose credits include The Deuce, Boardwalk Empire, Blue Bloods three Law & Order series and Grand Theft Auto V, died November 19. He was 66. His rep Jon Mason of Mason-Lewis Entertainment mentioned Carroll died suddenly while en route to a voice-over booking, but he did not provide a cause of death.

Born on May 21, 1960, Carroll appeared in features, television, short films and video games during a nearly three-decade screen career. His first screen credit was playing a cop in a 1998 episode of NBC’s Law & Order, and he would appear as other characters in three other episodes through 2004. He also had roles in two early-2000s episodes of its juggernaut spinoff Law & Order: SVU and two more in Law & Order: Criminal Intent that decade.

He would appear in a number of movies during the later 2000s and into the 2010s including Darren Aronfsky’s acclaimed 2009 drama The Wrestler, along with The Cake Eaters, The Capers, The Winning Season, The Hungry Ghosts, A Fish Story and the Robert De Niro-Kate Beckinsale pic Everything’s Fine, among others.

It has been revealed that carroll played Sheriff Victor Sickles in two 2012 episodes of HBO’s lauded period crime drama Boardwalk Empire, from Tenrence Winter and MArtin Scorsese and starring Steve Buscemi, appeared in episode of FX’s Glenn Close-Rose Byrne legal thriller Damages that same year. He went on to guest on NBC’s The Blacklist, CBS’ Blue Bloods, HBO’s High Maintenance, FX’s Pose and Netflix’s Marvel series The Punisher.

In a recent development, he landed perhaps his most recognizable role in 2017, recurring on the HBO’ ‘s The Deuce as Fat Mooney, who ran a New York City sex shop owned by Frankie Martino (James Franco). He appeared in a half-dozen episodes of the series about the rise of the porn industry in the 1970s and ’80s.

According to recent reports, most recently, Carroll filmed a role in A Delicate Arrangement, the upcoming film written and produced by Jayce Bartok and directed by Nick Sandow. It stars Carla Gugino as Vivien Leigh in the true story of two-time Oscar winning actress’ relationship with a Philadelphia florist (Matthew Modine). David Hyde Pierce also stars in the film, which is in post-production.

Recent findings suggest that “E.J. Carroll was a consummate actor known and loved for his intense commitment to the characters he played,” said who noted that Carroll was passionate about A Delicate Arrangement and helped ensure the project would be completed. “There isn’t an actor in New York that hadn’t worked with or crossed paths with E.J., known for stealing scenes alongside Robert De Niro, Mickey Rourke, Bruce Dern and most recently Jalen Brunson and Quinta Brunson. He will be greatly missed by the acting community which he lived for.”.

RELATED: Celebrities Who’ve Voiced Characters In ‘Grand Theft Auto’.

Carroll also voiced a character in the blockbuster 2013 video game Grand Theft Auto and played Dr. Scott in The Rocky Horror Tribute Show, a concert version of The Rocky Horror Show that played one night only in 2007 as a benefit for cancer charities Acting for a Cure/Komen for the Cure.

Information about survivors or a memorial service was not immediately available.

Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps.
  • Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable people to generate nonconsensual nude images.
  • According to the updated rules, apps that allow owners to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable people to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow owners to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow people to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

Industry observers note that A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of Latest Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same complications.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Industry observers note that update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple stated:.

Industry observers note that “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The firm added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

According to recent reports, just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company mentioned does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

In a recent development, as for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

In a recent development, apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

It has been revealed that update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps important issues and leaves out key context. The organization notes it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The company defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also says it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out newly introduced child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.
