#51205. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2959 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Industry observers note that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Industry observers note that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Industry observers note that the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully debuted on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

In a recent development, this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” indicates Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

It has been revealed that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

In a recent development, scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

It has been revealed that more than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a fresh rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

Recent findings suggest that if all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” indicates Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

Industry observers note that during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

It has been revealed that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu states, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Recent findings suggest that idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation highlights how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” indicates Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Industry observers note that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday claims.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday indicates Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Recent findings suggest that idefix’s interactions with its upcoming home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec notes. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

Sources indicate that what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel notes the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel states. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

It has been revealed that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu states.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

It has been revealed that during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

It has been revealed that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Recent findings suggest that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu claims. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

#51203. Tech Report: UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

Tech Report: UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the glitch ….
  • In a recent development, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the glitch ….

In a recent development, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Recent findings suggest that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

According to recent reports, in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

This would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve stated many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

Industry observers note that it would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the company found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple announced it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to new users and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

The iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal remarked. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it launched – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

According to recent reports, apple’s new HomeView just launched last Friday, but some early adopters reported complications with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems.

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following issue:.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

It’s unknown how many reports of Siri concerns on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta people. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

With HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a new issue you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now says: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

If you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView update, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

It’s understandable that complications might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, consumers might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (278 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Github

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L.
  • Sources indicate that the statement files at the top of lean/ give the definitions and state the theorems with sorry in place of their proofs; Solution.lean proves them from the library lean/Breakdown/.
  • The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L. Alpöge and T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it.

Sources indicate that the statement files at the top of lean/ give the definitions and state the theorems with sorry in place of their proofs; Solution.lean proves them from the library lean/Breakdown/. Each comparator*.json pairs a statement file with Solution.lean, names the theorems whose statements must agree, and permits only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.

The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and time.

The formalization contains no data. The certificate whose hash the paper gives is not in this repository; the paper says that it will be released. That the certificate satisfies the conditions of Appendix B is verified by a rigorous computation, involving interval arithmetic (128 bits of precision, with the Arb library through FLINT), which is not part of the formalization and is not in this repository either.

The source of the paper is not in this repository.

The package is the one of the paper's working repository, with one patch of 20 November 2026 applied to the cell-layer statements and to the library proofs that depend on them: the weight of one bound becomes $(|m|+\tfrac12)^2$ in place of $m^2+\tfrac14$, one constant of a cell may be zero, and the set of the harmonics of the model in a cell is restricted to those that do not vanish there. Appendix B of the paper states the conditions in this patched form. The patched package was not rebuilt when this repository was assembled.

  • The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what customers need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly states it has no aims for a native Mac app.

It has been revealed that you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft intends to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Sources indicate that planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

The June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Industry observers note that looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

In a recent development, microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

According to recent reports, does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

Sources indicate that “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team prepares. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED, 5:50 PM: A Los Angeles jury has convicted the man charged with setting the smoldering fire that later flared up into Palisades Fire that devastated Pacific Palisades and Malibu in early 2025. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was found guilty Friday of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

Industry observers note that rinderknecht faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in state prison when he is sentenced on March 17. He has been in federal custody since October 2025. See the bottom of this post for the the Justice Department’s detailed account of Rinderknecht’s movements on the night the first fire started and its case against him.

Back in June, a separate jury deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquitting Rinderknecht on similar charges including a third for timber set afire. Prosecutors dropped that last charge, and the In the new indictment, the first charge referred only to Rinderknecht’s setting of the Lachman Fire on New Year’s Eve, rather than the Lachman and Palisades fires. The Lachman Fire smoldered for a week before Santa Ana winds re-ignited the flames. Watch on Deadline.

During the just-ended trial, Assistant U.S. Attorney Matt O’Brien argued that Rinderknecht was consumed by anger, loneliness and a thirst for revenge, prompting him to use a grill lighter to ignite hilltop vegetation around midnight on Dec. 31, 2024, at the remote, deserted area adjacent to the Pacific Palisades’ Summit neighborhood. But defense lawyer Steven Haney argued there was no direct evidence proving that his client set the earlier fire, saying the prosecution’s case lacked any witnesses to the alleged crime and consisted only of circumstantial allegations.

Recent findings suggest that the Los Angeles Fire Department issued in a statement Friday after the verdict. “We respect the jury’s work and the long, difficult process that brought us to today’s verdict,” it reads in part. “Our first thought is with the families of those we lost and for everyone in our community whose lives were changed by this fire. No verdict, however important, could ever undo that loss.”.

The Palisades Fire was the most destructive blaze in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people, burning 23,448 acres, costing billions in damage and insurance claims, and ruining much of the exclusive Pacific Palisades community, destroying about 6,500 structures across the Palisades and Malibu. Read more details below, and see the full news release from the U.S. Department of Justice at the bottom of this post.

PREVIOUSLY, June 25: The jury charged with determining if Jonathan Rinderknecht is guilty of starting the blaze in early 2025 that became the devastating Palisades Fire can’t come up with a verdict, yet.

Recent findings suggest that “The jury in the Jonathan Rinderknecht trial sent a subsequent note saying they are deadlocked,” the Justice Department tells Deadline today. “The trial continues.”.

Recent findings suggest that how long the trial continues now or if a mistrial is declared becomes the vital questions. U.S. District Court Judge Anne Hwang has instructed the jury to return on Friday morning to take another kick at the can.

Industry observers note that A note from the jurors read out in court earlier this afternoon in downtown L.A. by the judge set the stage. “We have people on both sides that are dead set, unwavering and unwilling to change their opinion,” the note, the second of the day, noted. It went on to say: “We are at a standstill and unsure of how to proceed.”.

Ex-Uber driver Rinderknecht has always insisted he is innocent of the charges and being put up as a fall guy for the failures of civic leaders and First Responders. If a mistrial is declared in this instance, the feds could attempt another trial with a latest jury and hope for a better outcome.

Industry observers note that after just over a day of deliberations on the arson charges after a 10-day trial, the jurors indicated they had a verdict just over 90 minutes ago. The at the moment incarcerated Rinderknecht, his defense team, prosecutors and various local, state and federal officials were brought into court after the judge was informed there was a “unanimous verdict.”.

What they finally did hear left Judge Hwang in clear angst.

While there was some confusion initially over when their decision would be read out in court, and the clocked ticked away, it is now clear the case is in serious trouble — even as it continues.

Looking at up to 45 years behind bars if found guilty, Rinderknecht was, in Department of Justice documents filed last fall, “indicted on one count of Destruction of Property by Means of Fire (18 U.S.C. § 844(f)(1)); one count of Arson Affecting Property Used in Interstate Commerce (18 U.S.C. § 844(i)); and one count of Timber Set Afire (18 U.S.C. § 1855), in a case arising out of the Lachman/Palisades Fire in January 2025.”.

Today’s verdict or lack there of, will continue the frustration many feel over the wildfires, the response and the consequences. While some reconstruction has taken place in the Palisades, as well as Malibu and out of the Eaton Fire that tore through Altadena, progress has been slow and stymied by all metrics.

A major factor in the ongoing L.A. mayoral race, and the spark for the unsuccessful insurgency campaign of ex-Palisades resident and Hills alum Spencer Pratt, the fires and the fallout hang heavy over the city and the community as another sign of a metropolis that has lost its way — even more so this past week with the just extinguished cold storage warehouse fire in Boyle Heights that prompted air quality and other health warnings.

Industry observers note that the subject of an intense investigation by various branches of government both national and state, Rinderknecht was arrested in Florida on October 8 last year. The then 29-year-old is accused of intentionally starting a “hold over” fire the week before that eventually sparked into the Palisades Fire.

Placed at the scene by his own iPhone and failed 9-1-1 calls, Rinderknecht later that New Year’s Day morning drove away from the area as LAFD started arriving on the scene, making a gesture to assist the firefighters, the DOJ’s filing of last year asserted.

Industry observers note that A week later the same fire, which even after LAFD has been on the scene, had likely smoldered underground, reemerged and became known as the Palisades Fire. Destroying most of the Hollywood heavy community, the Palisades Fire killed more than a dozen people and decimated over 5,400 homes.

Sources indicate that earlier this week, after closing arguments, defense lawyer Steve Haney entered a motion to have the case dismissed based on lack of compelling evidence by the feds. With the bevy of online postings and asking AI platforms if you could start a fire with a lit cigarette, as well as Rinderknecht’s involvement with the January 1, 2025 Lachman Fire that preceded the Palisades Fire, that dismissal effort was dismissed pretty quickly by Judge Hwang.

More such motions from the defense may be in the offering ASAP if this deadlocked situation continues into next week.

Here is the Justice Department’s post-verdict news release:.

In a recent development, A former Los Angeles resident was found guilty by a jury today of starting what became the Palisades Fire of January 2025, the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, a.k.a. “Jonathan Rinder,” and “Jon Rinder,” was found guilty of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” mentioned Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”According to evidence presented at a 14-day trial, on January 1, 2025, Rinderknecht ignited what came to be known as the Lachman and Palisades fires.In the days leading up to the Lachman Fire, Rinderknecht exhibited extreme anger, indignation, and frustration about being unable to find companionship on Upcoming Year’s Eve 2024 and about a former co-worker whom he briefly dated in March 2024.Alone on New Year’s Eve, Rinderknecht drove several Uber passengers, nearly all of whom remembered him being angry that night. He dropped off his final Uber passenger in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles and drove to The Summit, a neighborhood where he had lived a few years earlier with a former lover.Rinderknecht drove towards Skull Rock Trailhead, parked his car, attempted to contact a former friend, and walked up the trail. He then used his iPhone to take videos at a nearby hilltop area and listened to a rap song – to which he had listened repeatedly in previous days – whose music video included things being lit on fire.When Rinderknecht maliciously started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, he was alone in a small clearing on Hidden Buddha Hill in Pacific Palisades.At approximately 12:12 a.m. on January 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman Fire had begun. During the next five minutes, Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of cellphone range. When he finally connected with 911, he was at the bottom of the hiking trail and reported the fire. By that point, a nearby resident already had reported the fire to authorities.Rinderknecht then fled in his car, passing fire engines driving in the opposite direction. He then turned around and followed the fire engines to the scene, driving at a high rate of speed. Rinderknecht walked up the same trail from earlier that night to watch the fire and the firefighters. At approximately 1:02 a.m., he used his iPhone to take more videos of the scene.During an interview with law enforcement on January 24, 2025, Rinderknecht lied about where he was when he first saw the Lachman Fire. He claimed he was near the bottom of a hiking trail when he first saw the fire and called 911, but geolocation data from his iPhone carrier indicated that he was standing in a clearing 30 feet from the fire as it rapidly grew.Although firefighters promptly suppressed the Lachman Fire, the fire continued to smolder and burn underground within the root structure of dense vegetation.On January 7, 2025, heavy winds caused the underground fire to surface and spread above ground in what became known as the Palisades Fire, which caused widespread damage in Pacific Palisades, killing 12 people, and destroyed 6,837 structures, causing an estimated $25 billion in damage in the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.United States District Judge Anne Hwang scheduled a March 17, 2027 sentencing hearing, at which time Rinderknecht would face a mandatory minimum sentence of five years in federal prison and a statutory maximum sentence of 40 years in federal prison.Rinderknecht has been in federal custody since October 2025.The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is investigating this matter with substantial assistance from the Los Angeles Police Department and the United States Forest Service.Assistant United States Attorneys Mark A. Williams, Matthew W. O’Brien, and Danbee C. Kim of the Environmental Crimes and Consumer Protection Section are prosecuting this case.If you are a victim of the Palisades Fire, updates about this criminal case can be found on this webpage.

Erik Pedersen and City News Service contributed to this report.

#51188. Fewer slides, more dragons

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1274 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Breakingchange ↗ Open Full Page

Fewer slides, more dragons

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Breakingchange

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here’s a familiar sight that could send a typical tech manager into hours of procrastination and avoidant behavior:.
  • Industry observers note that it starts with a simple ask for a meeting or a presentation.
  • And it gets worse when inevitably you need a coworker to contribute some content.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here’s a familiar sight that could send a typical tech manager into hours of procrastination and avoidant behavior:.

Industry observers note that it starts with a simple ask for a meeting or a presentation. No matter how pretty the template is, as soon as you decide you need “some slides,” you find yourself slinking down a path of obsessive pixel-pushing.

And it gets worse when inevitably you need a coworker to contribute some content. One understandably tries to cram as much text as possible into their space in 6pt font, while another (maybe a designer) prefers short sentences with bold words. You now get to make these look like they belong in the same presentation.

Five hours later, you have the perfect build, with diagrams and animations to make your slides more compelling, educational, and memorable. As you gaze upon your mediocre masterpiece, you wonder whether those hours were worth it.

You still need to communicate information with clarity, but maybe the medium has to change.

At Stripe, I have been accused of saying that we should ban slides. I may have remarked these words in anger after the fourth meeting of the week where my slides’ colors were slightly wrong because someone had pasted them in and had “matched styles in this presentation.” Most of the time, this may be an eyesore but doesn’t really matter; in this case, my green “on track” status badge had morphed into a dull yellow in the newly introduced theme.

I may not have meant it, but it’s an interesting provocation, especially when AI makes the alternatives much cheaper. Sometimes you have to take away the rotary phones to get people to use upcoming technology.

So, I decided to try banning myself from creating slides for any reason, forcing myself to use AI to create interactive presentations instead.

Without much effort (and in under 30 minutes), you can create a Bauhaus-themed interactive strategy explainer….

Or a planetary system explaining what your team does….

This experiment has been surprisingly successful. Tired and busy Zoom brains might immediately check out when they see a slide deck, but a planetary system! Wow! That catches their attention long enough to get your point across, making meetings much more fun and efficient. And after the meeting, you can send them a link to explore the solar system on their own time. They may accidentally internalize your key points as they’re playing around with it. 🙂.

With traditional slide decks, collaboration feels like a burden. Someone might mess up your template, or use the wrong font. At the end of the day, despite your efforts, slides made by different people who own just one section will likely result in a jarring experience (or at best a “mid” experience).

Sources indicate that on the other hand, everyone has fun building low-stakes, vibe-coded webpages together. I can ask my agent to fix the layout instead of moving everything around myself. I found that after folks see others doing it, they do it themselves because it saves time while allowing them to be more creative.

Moving towards the extreme end of collaboration, I created a village of cross-org tech leads as an icebreaker exercise for an onsite. I was nervous about how it’d go given how many humans and their agents were contributing, but folks seemed to enjoy vibe-adding themselves to our tech lead village, and an old, non-AI innovation called git kept everyone’s contributions manageable.

And they kept adding to it as the day progressed.

In a recent development, it started with a tech lead from Risk adding a dungeon and a dragon to represent the dragons the team slays for us. Inspired by that customization, others started to add their own. By the end of the day, there was a Live MaaS sign and the Pacifica Taco Bell representing the MaaS (Money as a Service) team. There was also a DEEP lake representing DEEP (Developer & End-user Experience Platform), filled with DEEP sea creatures.

Someone eventually added a way for tech leads to explore other teams, so we could see the inside of the Risk dungeon, the Pacifica Taco Bell, and the DEEP lake.

This was the first time I’d seen people engage with the creation of an icebreaker activity or presentation beyond the bounds of the activity itself. Like, it’s literally fun to code with your coworkers and riff off of each other’s ideas. It’s all low-stakes code, and our agents help us write it and make small tweaks. If a different metaphor or idea comes to mind, you can ~easily and ~cheaply start from scratch.

The village icebreaker got me rethinking other group activities I’d traditionally done in slides or Figma. Here’s a fun storybook holiday book exchange that I previously would have run in Figma, but is now interactive and ~infinitely customizable. If you’re at Stripe, you can just point your agent at the linked AGENTS.md and ask it to build one for your team on our internal infra.

This is basically just “how to vibe code a basic webpage with your friends,” but it’s worth writing down, as I find that folks sometimes hold themselves back from applying AI to well-understood use cases like creating compelling presentations.

I am impatient, so I prefer simplicity above all else. In fact, I find that simple prompts work best for divergent work like brainstorming, naming, or picking a visual direction. To that end, there’s nothing super fancy or really even a “workflow” to tell you about here. I asked my agent to put these steps together:.

It has been revealed that have an idea you want to present. This is the most key part. Maybe it’s a doc, some quick bullets, or a stream of consciousness you sloppily typed on your phone on the ferry ride into the office.

It has been revealed that ask your coding agent for a few ways to explain it. Maybe it’s a lifecycle, a planetary system, or something you haven’t thought of. Have it make quick mocks so you can see what works. (You can repeat this step until you’re happy with the concept.).

Industry observers note that pick a concept and play with the visual style. I’m a fan of pixel art and Bauhaus, but you can ask your agent to cook up a few directions. Repeat until you find something you like.

In a recent development, build it and iterate. Ask your agent to change the content, tweak the visuals, or add interactions and animations. You can get much more creative than you could in slides without moving every little thing yourself.

Make it easy for others to contribute. Ask your agent to create an AGENTS.md explaining how the project works and how to contribute. Then your coworkers and their agents can take it from there.

You can keep going forever, of course. I stop when I have something that gets the idea across. For me, this consistently takes less time than making slides, and my agent can crank away on iterations in the background.

If you’re just presenting, you can run it locally; you only need to deploy it if you want others to explore on their own. And if you need presenter mode with your script, just ask your agent to build it.

In a recent development, my pithy learning from this experiment: AI can help us create conditions for creativity to emerge, even when doing pre-singularity activities like presentation creation and icebreakers. When you make something people want to engage with, it unlocks more ideas, opens more doors, and hatches more dragons than a slide deck ever could.

According to recent reports, halide 3.4 is out today as the latest update to the pro camera app. The update adds several new features, including a larger viewfinder for iPhone Duo and more.

In a recent development, the new Halide upgrade also lets you use the outer screen on iPhone Duo as a live preview or a fill flash. It brings back a few camera tools from Halide Mark II as well.

Lux Optics first added iPhone Duo support in October with Halide 3.3. With the phone fully open, the initial iPhone Duo revision let you review your most recent photo alongside the live viewfinder.

Today’s latest XL mode gives you the option to swap the photo preview for a larger viewfinder. Controls on both sides enable two-handed shooting.

While the Duo is open, the outer screen can mirror Halide’s camera controls or show a full-screen viewfinder without controls. The second option lets the person you’re photographing see how you’ve framed the shot.

In low light, Halide can use the outer screen as a fill flash. That gives you a softer source of light for portraits, and Halide’s developers recommend turning the screen brightness all the way up before taking the photo.

According to recent reports, halide also now places the histogram along the Duo’s crease. The revision revises the Photo Lab interface for editing with the Duo half open as well.

On other iPhones, Halide 3.4 restores the color and luminance histograms and the shutter timer from Mark II.

Industry observers note that halide Mark III launched back in May with a redesigned camera and the fresh Photo Lab editor. Recent updates added RAW-only capture in 3.1 and Aperture Priority for iPhone 18 Pro in 3.2. Halide Mark III version 3.4 is available now on the App Store.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of new features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

In a recent development, but Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a upcoming setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

While wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

Latest in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

In a recent development, you can also move the new slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.
